headline: Approved projects at 80 Seventh Avenue, 128 Lilley Avenue, 22 Olde Canal Drive; continued 123 University Avenue to October 15.
summary: Petitions covered variances and one special permit. Five projects were approved: 38 & 49 Casco Street, 80 Seventh Avenue, 12-14 Tolman Avenue, 128 Lilley Avenue, and 22 Olde Canal Drive. The request for 123 University Avenue was continued to October 15.
decisions: Continued the TLGLE, LLC variance request for 123 University Avenue to the October 15 meeting, 5-0.
Approved the variance for Ideal Living Home Development, Inc. at 38 & 49 Casco Street with a condition that the applicant comply with Engineering Department comments, 5-0.
Approved the variance for Michael Brown at 80 Seventh Avenue with three conditions, 5-0.
Approved the variance for Igor Jorge at 12-14 Tolman Avenue, 5-0.
Approved the variance for Felix Ramos at 128 Lilley Avenue, 5-0.
Approved the special permit for Metro Sign & Awning at 22 Olde Canal Drive, with illumination allowed from 1 hr after sunrise to 1 hr after closing, 5-0.

plain_text:
Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals Minutes 
8/10/2026 at 6:30 P.M.  
 
Note: These minutes are not completed verbatim. For further detail, contact the Division of 
Development Services, 375 Merrimack Street, Lowell, MA or refer to video recordings available online 
at www.LTC.org. 
 
Members Present: Chairman Pech, Vice Chair Callahan, Member McCarthy, Member Procope, Member 
Hovey, Member Shanahan 
 
Members Absent: Member Briere 
 
Others Present: Dylan Ricker, Senior Planner 
 
The following represents the actions taken by the Zoning Board of Appeals at the 8/10/2026 meeting. This 
meeting was held in the  City Council Chamber . Attendees had the ability to participate via Zoom as 
permitted by Chapter 2 of the Acts of 2025, signed into law on March 28, 2025. 
 
Chairman Pech called the meeting to order at 6:30 PM. 
I. Continued Business 
 
ZBA-2026-15 
Petition Type: Variance  
Applicant: TLGLE, LLC 
Property Located at: 123 University Avenue, 01854 
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Section 6.1 
Petition: The Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals will hold a public hearing to hear all interested persons 
relative to an application by TLGLE, LLC to convert the existing building at 123 University Avenue into two 
(2) ground-floor commercial units, and twelve (12) stud io apartments. The subject property is located in 
the Traditional Mixed-Use (TMU) zoning district. The proposal requires Variance approval per Section 6.1 
for relief from the minimum off -street parking requirement, and for any other relief under the Lowell 
Zoning Ordinance. 
 
On Behalf: 
None 
 
Speaking in Opposition:  
None 
 
Speaking in Favor: 
None
Discussion: 
V. Pech said the ZBA got communication that the applicant is requesting a continuance to the October 
15th hearing date. V. Pech asked about the opinion of Board members. 
 
S. Callahan asked why the request was made. T . Hovey said the applicant is sca ling down the project to 
require less parking. 
 
D. McCarthy said he would not be supportive of granting an additional variance. S . Callahan noted the 
applicant signed the continuance form waiving the Board decision time limit. V . Pech said this should be 
the final continuance. 
 
Motion: 
D. McCarthy motioned to continue to the October 15 th ZBA meeting. S . Callahan seconded the motion. 
The motion passed unanimously, (5-0). 
 
ZBA-2026-24 
Petition Type: Variance  
Applicant: Ideal Living Home Development, Inc. 
Property Located at: 38 & 49 Casco Street, 01854 
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Section 5.1  
Petition: The Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals will hold a public hearing to hear all interested persons 
relative to an application by Ideal Living Home Development, Inc to construct a single-family home in the 
Traditional Single -Family (TSF) zoning district at 38 & 49 Casco Street. The project requires Variance 
approval per Section 5.1 for relief from the minimum  frontage requirement, and for any other relief 
required under the Lowell Zoning Ordinance. 
 
On Behalf: 
Emerlyn Gonzalez, Applicant 
 
E. Gonzalez said they are looking to renew the Variance to start the project. E . Gonzalez said there were 
no changes from the original approval, and they are before the Board because the approval expired.  
 
Speaking in Opposition:  
None 
 
Speaking in Favor: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
G. Procope asked if the applicant addressed the Engineering Dept comment regarding the grinder pump. 
E. Gonzalez said once she has these documents she will forward those over. G . Procope noted the 
engineering comments, G . Procope said this comment will need to be addressed before granting full 
approval. G . Procope said addressing this c omment should be a condition of approval. G . Procope 
expressed support for the proposal. 
 
T. Hovey said he remains in favor of the petition.
D. McCarthy said the relief requested is reasonable and noted there is no opposition present. D. McCarthy 
asked why the project was not able to be started before expiration. E. Gonzalez said they were not aware 
of the expiration which is why the approval expired. D. McCarthy expressed support. 
 
S. Callahan said he has no comments or concerns, and expressed support. S . Callahan said the relief 
requested is reasonable.  
 
D. Shanahan noted there are no substantial changes, and expressed support. D . Shanahan said the 
engineering comments were not relevant to the Variance and is unsure if this should be a condition. 
 
V. Pech said he has no concerns. V. Pech asked if the engineering condition is acceptable, E. Gonzalez said 
yes. 
 
D. McCarthy said the plan was missing a detail requested by engineers which is why he feels this should 
be added as a condition. 
 
Motion: 
D. McCarthy motioned to approve with the following condition: 
1. The applicant shall comply with the Engineering Department comments. 
 G. Procope seconded the motion. The motion passed unanimously, (5-0). 
 
ZBA-2026-28 
Petition Type: Variance  
Applicant: Michael Brown 
Property Located at: 80 Seventh Avenue, 01854 
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Section 5.1  
Petition: The Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals will hold a public hearing to hear all interested persons 
relative to an application by Michael Brown to construct a single-family home at 80 Seventh Avenue. The 
subject property is located in the Traditional Single -family (TSF) zoning district. The proposal requires 
Variance approval per Section 5.1 for relief from the minimum frontage, and maximum front yard setback 
requirements, and for any other relief required under the Lowell Zoning Ordinance. 
 
On Behalf: 
Ken Lania, Applicant’s Engineer  
 
K. Lania explained the proposed project, and proposed layout. K . Lania said the goal is to subdivide the 
rear lot to build a new home for a family member. K. Lania said they are doing a similar subdivision to the 
abutting parcels that was done in 2000 and 2002. K . Lania said the rear lot will have 25 ft of frontage 
utilizing the existing driveway, and  said there will be an access easement. K . Lania said the existing 
structure will remain the same. K. Lania said the shape of the land impacts the development, and said the 
proposal is consistent with the neighborhood. K. Lania said a new sewer connection and water connection 
were installed because the road was recently repaved.  
 
Michael Brown, Applicant 
 
Speaking in Opposition:
Robert Jussaume, 90 Seventh Avenue 
 
R. Jussaume said his concern is related to the configuration of the lot and substantial zoning relief 
required. R. Jussaume said the rear lot would only have 25 ft of frontage and would be setback significantly 
from the street. R. Jussaume said the 90 and 94 Seventh Ave lots are different because each has their own 
access to Seventh Ave. R. Jussaume said the home is located in the backyard and has concerns about the 
upper story windows viewing into abutting backyards. R. Jussaume said the applicant should reorient the 
facade to reduce this impact. R . Jussaume said screening may help, but privacy issues from the second 
story and orientation of the home  will still exist . R . Jussaume expressed concerns with drainage and 
requested information on where water runoff will travel. R. Jussaume said 94 Seventh Ave relies on a well 
for water, and expressed concern about its impacts on groundwater. R. Jussaume expressed concern that 
the application includes language about 4 additional  dwelling units, and asked the applicant to confirm 
the number of dwelling units proposed. R. Jussaume said the applicant should consider another site layout 
to reduce impacts on neighbors.  
 
Susan Jussaume, 90 94 Seventh Avenue 
 
S. Jussaume expressed concern about the impacts of the new building. S . Jussaume said her home was 
originally meant to connect to Eighth Ave before the condos were constructed. S. Jussaume said they are 
looking to protect their own property to keep green space on the abutting property. S . Jussaume said 
there is ledge in the area. S. Jussaume expressed concern with lights. S . Jussaume expressed concern 
about language in the application stating there are 4 units proposed. S. Jussaume expressed concern with 
potential blasting. S. Jussaume expressed concerns about utilities, and the location of the home. S . 
Jussaume said utilities should be placed underground. S. Jussaume expressed concerns about car fumes.  
 
Kaedra Walsh, 70 Seventh Avenue 
 
K. Walsh said 4 homes would change the neighborhood and expressed concern. K . Walsh said the 
applicant could construct an ADU if they are looking to move family in. K. Walsh expressed concern about 
tree removal and said there was not drainage mitigation. K. Walsh asked for info on drainage mitigation. 
K. Walsh requested no easement within 15 feet of her property line.  
 
Speaking in Favor: 
Corey Belanger, 200 Rogers Street 
 
C. Belanger expressed support for the proposal. C. Belanger said the applicant was originally a restaurant 
owner not a developer. C . Belanger said this home will be occupied by his family. C . Belanger expressed 
support for the petition.  
 
Discussion: 
K. Lania said the application is just for a single-family home. K. Lania said there is a typo that says 4 units 
and said the applicant is only seeking a single -family home. K . Lania said the structure has a proposed 
basement and deep hole testing was done. K. Lania said they will do their best to avoid ledge, and would 
not want to conduct blasting. K . Lania said the area is very large, and said he believes they can find a 
location without ledge. K . Lania said it would be possible to raise the home to avoid ledge. K . Lania said 
the applicant will still need a subdivision approval from the Planning Board and some of the ut ilities will 
be reviewed then. K. Lania said they will be doing a rain garden and retaining all stormwater from the new 
home via stormwater detention system. K . Lania said they can coordinate with the abutters prior to
construction to reconfigure the home. K . Lania said the windows can be reconfigured. K . Lania said 
headlights would not shine into the abutting property but they are amenable to installing a fence. K. Lania 
said utilities will go up 25 ft wide access way. K. Lania said they are using the existing driveway due to the 
topography of the lot.  
 
T. Hovey expressed concerns about the hatchet designed subdivision. T. Hovey said his design preferences 
aren’t relevant to the petition. T. Hovey said the Variance is for frontage and max front yard setback and 
the decision must be based on facts. T. Hovey said more discussion between the abutters and homeowner 
should take place. T. Hovey said based on the facts of the petition he is not opposed to the project.  
 
D. McCarthy thanked the abutters for speaking on the project. D . McCarthy noted the existing distances 
from property lines, and said the new home exceeds the setback d istance from existing structures. K . 
Lania said the existing lot is 30,000 sq ft. D. McCarthy noted only 7500 sq ft is required for a single-family 
home. D. McCarthy said the applicant should submit revised documents stating it is a single-family home. 
D. McCarthy expressed support for a solid 6 ft privacy fence around the property. K . Lania agreed. D. 
McCarthy said the engineering concerns should be addressed by the Planning Board. 
 
D. McCarthy asked about adding a shade tree. K . Lania agreed. D. McCarthy asked how many trees are 
being removed. K. Lania said no trees will be removed. D. McCarthy expressed support. 
 
S. Callahan thanked the abutters for appearing. S . Callahan noted the substantial hardship criteria is no 
longer in effect and noted the practical difficulty criteria is now in effect. S . Callahan said the layout is 
reasonable and is similar to the abutting property. S. Callahan said the project meets the practical difficulty 
standard for a Variance. S. Callahan said the project meets the criteria for a Variance. 
 
D. Shanahan thanked the abutters. D. Shanahan noted this is someone else’s property and the Board must 
review the project on the Variance criteria. D. Shanahan said the proposed home is a nice home, and said 
any noise issues is a neighbor issue. D. Shanahan expressed support. 
 
G. Procope thanked neighbors for appearing. G. Procope noted the development is only 1 unit. G. Procope 
expressed support. G. Procope said the developer should adhere to the concerns of the neighbors.  
 
V. Pech thanked the neighbors for appearing. V. Pech said the concerns were addressed by the applicant, 
and noted the home is for family. V . Pech expressed support. V. Pech noted the conditions proposed. K . 
Lania agreed. 
 
S. Callahan added the engineering comments should be added as a condition of approval. D . McCarthy 
noted the wastewater comments stated  they will need an agreement between the neighbors. K . Lania 
said the agreement is from the owner to the owner.  D. McCarthy said it does not need to be a condition. 
 
D. McCarthy said the conditions are the revised documents to show it is for a 1 family, to provide a new 
shade tree, and to provide a 6ft fence to screen the new driveway. 
 
Motion: 
D. McCarthy motioned to approve with the following conditions: 
1. The applicant shall submit revised documents confirming they are proposing only a single -family 
home;
2. The applicant shall plant a new shade tree; and 
3. The applicant shall provide a 6 ft privacy fence to screen the new driveway. 
S. Callahan seconded the motion. The motion passed unanimously, (5-0). 
 
II. New Business 
 
ZBA-2026-30 
Petition Type: Variance  
Applicant: Igor Jorge 
Property Located at: 12-14 Tolman Avenue, 01854 
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Section 5.1  
Petition: The Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals will hold a public hearing to hear all interested persons 
relative to an application by Igor Jorge to construct an addition and a new deck at 12-14 Tolman Avenue. 
The subject property is located in the Traditional Single-Family (TSF) zoning district. The proposal requires 
Variance approval per Section 5.1 for relief from the maximum floor area ratio (FAR), and any other relief 
required under the Lowell Zoning Ordinance. 
 
On Behalf: 
Igor Jorge, Applicant 
 
I. Jorge said he is looking to construct an addition at his property to extend his kitchen.  
 
Speaking in Opposition:  
None 
 
Speaking in Favor: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
D. McCarthy thanked the applicant for taking care of the property, and noted the challenges with the floor 
plan. D. McCarthy said the addition does not have a significant impact on the property, and said the relief 
requested is minimal. D. McCarthy expressed support. 
 
S. Callahan said he has no concerns, and said the addition is modest. S. Callahan expressed support. 
 
D. Shanahan expressed support, and said he has no comments or questions. 
 
G. Procope said the property owner is improving the property, and said the relief requested is minimal. 
G. Procope expressed support. 
 
T. Hovey expressed support. 
 
V. Pech expressed support, and said it improves the neighborhood. 
 
Motion: 
D. McCarthy motioned to approve, the motion was seconded by G. Procope . The motion passed 
unanimously, (5-0).
ZBA-2026-31 
Petition Type: Variance   
Applicant: Felix Ramos  
Property Located at: 128 Lilley Avenue, 01852 
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Section 5.1   
Petition: The Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals will hold a public hearing to hear all interested persons 
relative to an application by Felix Ramos to construct two new decks at 128 Lilley Avenue. The subject 
property is located in the Traditional Two-Family (TTF) zoning district. The proposal requires Variance 
approval per Section 5.1 for relief from the minimum side yard setback requirement, and for any other 
relief required under the Lowell Zoning Ordinance. 
 
On Behalf: 
Unknown, Applicant 
 
The applicant said the decks are 2 feet from the setbacks, and there will be new deck. The applicant said 
the new deck will be connected to the existing deck and needs 8 ft of relief. 
 
Speaking in Opposition:  
None 
 
Speaking in Favor: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
S. Callahan said he has no concerns, and expressed support. 
 
D. Shanahan said the setback is common in this portion of Centralville, and said the work will improve the 
neighborhood. The applicant said the home had to be rebuilt due to fire. D. Shanahan expressed support. 
 
G. Procope expressed support. 
 
T. Hovey said he has no questions. 
 
D. McCarthy said the plot plan shows a new deck being 10 ft 2 in, and asked if that is 10 x 20 overall. The 
applicant said the new deck is 20 x 11. The applicant said the existing deck is 10 ft 2in. D. McCarthy asked 
if 12 ft is being added. The applicant confirmed. D. McCarthy noted the existing is non -conforming, and 
said that nonconformity is being extended back. The applicant confirmed. D. McCarthy agreed that the 
relief is reasonable. D. McCarthy asked if it is a two or three family. The applicant said it is a two family. 
 
V. Pech said her has no concerns and improves the neighborhood. 
 
Motion: 
D. McCarthy motioned to approve. G. Procope seconded the motion. The motion passed unanimously, 
(5-0). 
 
ZBA-2026-32 
Petition Type: Special Permit
Applicant: Metro Sign & Awning 
Property Located at: 22 Olde Canal Drive, 01851 
Applicable Zoning Bylaws: Section 6.3 
Petition: The Lowell Zoning Board of Appeals will hold a public hearing to hear all interested persons 
relative to an application by Metro Sign & Awning to install an internally illuminated sign at 22 Olde 
Canal Drive. The property is located in the Light Industrial (LI) zoning district. The proposal requires 
Special Permit approval per Section 6.3 for internally illuminated signage, and for any other relief 
required under the Lowell Zoning Ordinance. 
 
On Behalf: 
Cliff Conte, Applicant 
 
C. Conte said they are seeking a Special Permit and noted a permit was issued to put the unlit sign up. C . 
Conte said they are seeking approval to light the sign. C. Conte said the sign does not face any properties 
and it is not excessively bright. 
 
Speaking in Opposition:  
None 
 
Speaking in Favor: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
D. Shanahan said the area is a very commercial area and expressed support. 
 
G. Procope said he has no questions and expressed support. 
 
T. Hovey said he has no questions. 
 
D. McCarthy asked for the hours of operation for the business. C . Conte said he is unsure, and said it is a 
healthcare facility that helps people back into society. D. McCarthy said in the past illuminated signs were 
restricted from 1 hr before sunrise to 1 hr after closing.  
 
S. Callahan said he has no questions or concerns and would just like a condition on the hours of 
illumination. 
 
V. Pech said he has no concerns. 
 
Motion: 
D. McCarthy motioned to approve with the condition that the hours of illum ination shall be 1 hr after 
sunrise to 1 hr after closing. S. Callahan seconded the motion. The motion passed unanimously, (5-0). 
 
III. Other Business 
Minutes for Approval:   
7/13/2026
D. McCarthy motioned, and S. Callahan seconded the motion to approve the meeting minutes. The motion 
passed unanimously (5-0). 
 
S. Callahan noted the changes to the Variance criteria and requested a Law update. D. Ricker said Law will 
be providing an update.  
 
S. Callahan congratulated the Smith Baker Center on their progress and said he is looking forward to their 
progress. 
 
Adjournment  
D. McCarthy motioned to adjourn. S. Callahan seconded. The motion passed unanimously (5-0). 
 
Meeting adjourned at 7:52 PM.
